- `src/audit/audit-query.mjs:41,49-51`, `src/platform/listing.mjs:1`: `summarizeActors` counts only the first `limit` matches instead of every match. Governing spec `governing-spec.md` "Selection and counting" says: "An actor summary takes a query that is valid under the audit query rules, `limit` included, and counts every entry it matches, ignoring `limit`, as `{actor, entries}`". The implementation calls `selectEntries(entries, query, at)`, which is `pageOf(entries, ..., byTime, query)`, and `pageOf` applies `.slice(0, page.limit)`. With `limit: 1` and several matching entries, the actor counts are truncated, so the summary is wrong. Fix: count the matches through a predicate-only filter that does not apply `limit`, for example `entries.filter(...)` in `summarizeActors`, keeping `limit` only for the query validation in `prepareQuery`.

- `src/badges/badge-service.mjs:5-6,16`, `src/platform/append-log.mjs:6-8`: the eventKey idempotency lookup is limited to the event's own building. Governing spec `governing-spec.md` "Request keys" says: "if an event recorded in any building has the key, recording returns it and does no further work." `findKeyedEvent` calls `store.list(event)`, and `append-log.mjs` `list({buildingId})` filters `record.buildingId === buildingId`. A badge event whose `eventKey` was already recorded under a different building is therefore appended again instead of returning the stored event. Fix: look up the key across all buildings, for example by listing the store without a building filter before the repeat and building checks.

- `src/billing/invoice-request.mjs:12`: a credit reason is stored trimmed, but the spec requires it stored as supplied. Governing spec "Invoices" says: "its `reason` must not be blank after trimming; the reason is stored exactly as supplied." `prepareCredit` returns `reason: credit.reason.trim()`, so a reason such as `" goodwill "` is saved as `"goodwill"`, which changes the stored credit record. Fix: validate with `trimmed(credit.reason)` but return `reason: credit.reason` unchanged.

- `src/exports/csv-format.mjs:7`: the CSV quoting doubles only the first inner double quote. Governing spec "CSV exports" says: "A field containing a comma, double quote, carriage return or line feed is wrapped in double quotes, with inner double quotes doubled". `text.replace(/"/, '""')` has no `g` flag, so a value such as `say "hi" now` becomes `"say ""hi" now"`, which is malformed CSV. Fix: use `text.replace(/"/g, '""')`.

- `src/exports/value-format.mjs:29`: list items are passed through the text formula-prefix rule. Governing spec "CSV exports" says: "a `list` of strings is joined with `;`, its items written as stored." `formatList` runs `value.map(formatText)`, which prefixes items beginning with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` with `'`, so `["=SUM(A1)"]` is written as `'=SUM(A1)` instead of `=SUM(A1)`. Fix: use `value.join(';')` after the type check, without `formatText`.

- `src/members/allowance.mjs:12`, `src/platform/periods.mjs:5`: a reservation whose `startAt` equals the first instant of the usage month is excluded from the allowance. Governing spec "Selection and counting" says: "A member's used minutes are the total length in minutes of the member's `confirmed` reservations whose `startAt` is within the month", and "Usage month is a half-open UTC calendar month" in "Time limits and expiry". `overlaps(instant(startAt), period)` evaluates `right.startAt < left.endAt`, i.e. `period.startAt < startAt`, so a reservation starting exactly at `Date.UTC(year, month - 1, 1)` is not counted. Fix: test `period.startAt <= reservation.startAt && reservation.startAt < period.endAt` directly, for example with `contains`-style logic instead of the strict overlap helper.

- `src/messaging/messaging-service.mjs:54-56`: a non-quiet message is sent before its save has completed. Governing spec "Message delivery" says: "A message created outside quiet hours is saved as `sent` with `sentAt` from `now()` before `send` receives `{messageId, memberId, body}`", and "Saving before notifying" repeats it. `const saved = store.save(sent);` is not awaited, so `send(sentNotice(sent))` runs while the store write is still queued. A failed save is also detached from the caller. Fix: `const saved = await store.save(sent); await send(sentNotice(saved));` and return `saved`.

- `src/messaging/quiet-hours.mjs:35`: `releaseTime` returns one minute too late for instants that are not on a minute boundary. Governing spec "Message delivery" says the release is "at the first minute boundary after `now()` whose local minute is `endMinute`". With offset `0`, `now` = `10:00:30` and `endMinute` = `601`, the first boundary after `now` with local minute 601 is `10:01:00`. The code computes `minuteStart(at + MINUTE - 1)` = `10:01:00` and then adds `wait` = 1, returning `10:02:00`. The same error applies when `endMinute` equals the current local minute: with `now` = `10:00:30` and `endMinute` = `600`, the code releases at `10:01:00`, while the spec requires the next day at `10:00:00`. Fix: compute the candidate as the boundary of the next minute, `const next = minuteStart(at) + MINUTE`, and set `wait` to `((endMinute - localMinute(next) + DAY) % DAY)`, so that the boundary's local minute is `endMinute`.

- `src/reservations/transitions.mjs:16-17`: `applyTransition` mutates the history array of the record it receives. Governing spec "Workspace Reservation Contract" says in its Conventions: "Operations never modify a reservation object they receive; they return new records." `const next = {...record, state: rule.to};` copies the object but not `history`, so `next.history.push({state: rule.to, at})` appends to the caller's `record.history`. A rejected or repeated caller copy, a confirm followed by a cancel on the original object, or a reschedule on the same object all show the extra entry. Fix: build the new history immutably, for example `const next = {...record, state: rule.to, history: [...record.history, {state: rule.to, at}]};`.

- `src/reservations/reservation-service.mjs:53-57`: `rescheduleReservation` does not apply the duration limit to the new window. Governing spec "Rescheduling" says: "The new window must have an `endAt` value later than its `startAt` value. It is then snapped, and the snapped window must satisfy the duration limit and be available." The function checks `endAt <= startAt`, snaps the window, and checks availability, but never calls `exceedsMaxDuration` (which `createReservation` uses for the same rule at `src/reservations/reservation-service.mjs` with `exceedsMaxDuration(window)`). A reschedule to a 300-minute window is therefore saved, although the spec limits the snapped window to 240 minutes. Fix: after `snapWindow`, add `if (exceedsMaxDuration(window)) throw new Error('reservation is too long');` before the availability check.

- `src/reservations/catalog.mjs:16`: `hasAmenities` compares a set size with the raw array length, so a room whose `amenities` list repeats a name cannot be booked, even when no amenity is requested. Governing spec "Rooms" says: "a room must contain every requested amenity." With `room.amenities = ['wifi', 'wifi']` and `amenities = []`, `new Set(['wifi','wifi']).size` is 1 while `room.amenities.length` is 2, so `hasAmenities` returns false and `createReservation` throws "requested amenities are unavailable". `listEligibleRooms` also excludes the room. Fix: compare against the deduplicated room set, for example `amenities.every((amenity) => room.amenities.includes(amenity))`.

- `src/schedules/closures.mjs:26`, used at `src/schedules/front-desk-service.mjs:31` and `:56`: `hasEnded` truncates the difference to whole minutes, so a closure that ends less than a minute from now counts as ended. Governing spec "Desk closures" in "Time limits and expiry" says: "A closure whose `endAt` is not later than `now()` is rejected." and "Upcoming desk closures are the building's active closures whose `endAt` is later than `now()`". `minutesBetween(at, endAt)` is `Math.trunc((endAt - at) / MINUTE)`, so `endAt = at + 30000` gives 0 and `hasEnded` returns true. `addClosure` then rejects a closure that is still in effect, and `upcomingClosures` omits it. Fix: compare the instants directly, `closure.endAt <= at`.

- `src/utilization/room-directory.mjs:7,10,36`: a report room entry with no `active` field is selected as active. Governing spec "Selection and counting" says: "only rooms whose `active` value is `true` and that contain every requested amenity are selected." `ENTRY_DEFAULTS = Object.freeze({active: true, amenities: []})` (line 7) and `const room = {...ENTRY_DEFAULTS, ...entry};` (line 10) turn a missing `active` into `true`, and `loadDirectory` (line 36) then keeps it through `room.active === true`. The spec only admits a room whose `active` value is `true`, so an entry that omits the field must be excluded. Fix: remove `active` from `ENTRY_DEFAULTS`, or default it to `false`, so that only an explicit `true` is selected.

- `src/waitlist/waitlist-service.mjs:60-61`: `acceptOffer` accepts an expired offer. Governing spec "Waitlist" says: "Only a nonexpired `offered` entry may be accepted; acceptance sets `accepted` and `acceptedAt` and books nothing." Also "Time limits and expiry": "A waitlist offer is expired when `now()` is equal to or later than its `expiresAt`." `moveEntry(entry, 'accept', at)` returns an entry whose `state` is already `accepted`, and `isLapsing(next, at)` requires `next.state === 'offered'`, so the check is always false and the expired offer is saved as accepted. Fix: test the original entry before the transition, for example `if (isLapsing(entry, at)) throw new Error('offer has expired');` or `if (isExpired(entry, at))` with the `offered` state check, before calling `moveEntry`.

- `src/waitlist/entry-states.mjs:9,22`: the withdrawal cutoff applies to `waiting` entries as well as `offered` ones. Governing spec "Time limits and expiry" says: "Withdrawing an `offered` waitlist entry is rejected when its `startAt` is less than 60 minutes after `now()`. A `waiting` entry has no such limit." The rule `{action: 'withdraw', from: ['waiting', 'offered'], ..., cutoff: WITHDRAW_CUTOFF_MINUTES}` applies `if (rule.cutoff !== undefined && entry.startAt - at < minutes(rule.cutoff)) throw` to both states, so a `waiting` entry starting in 30 minutes cannot be withdrawn. Fix: split the rule so the cutoff is set only for `from: ['offered']`, and keep a separate unrestricted rule for `waiting`.

- `src/payments/payment-service.mjs:54` with `src/payments/payment-policy.mjs:53-55`: `paid` is always 0. Governing spec "Time limits and expiry" says: "A payment status reports `dueAt`, `late` and `paid`, the sum of `captured` minus `refunded` over its `captured` and `refunded` intents." `netPaid(intents, invoiceId)` compares `intent.invoiceId === invoiceId`, but `paymentStatus` passes the whole `current` invoice object (`{...invoice, id}`) as `invoiceId`, not `current.id`, so no intent matches. An invoice with a captured 500 and no refund is reported as `paid: 0`. Fix: pass the id, `netPaid(await store.list(), current.id)`.
